reference.title: Talking about people from different countries
reference.text: We usually use the + nationality adjective + -s to talk about the people from a country, e.g. the Americans, the Belgians. If the nationality adjective ends with /s/, /z/, /ʃ/, or /tʃ/, we don’t add -s, e.g. the English, the Chinese, the Dutch. For some countries there is a special word for the people, e.g. Poland > the Poles, Turkey > the Turks.

reference.why: No -s after adjectives ending in /s/, /z/, /ʃ/, /tʃ/: the Chinese, the Swiss, the French.
Some countries have a special word for the people: the Poles, the Turks.

reference.title: Active or passive?
reference.text: Alfred Nobel invented dynamite. (active – the focus is on Alfred Nobel) Dynamite was invented by Alfred Nobel. (passive – the focus is on dynamite). We often use the passive when it isn’t known or isn’t important who does or did the action: My car was stolen last week. Volvo cars are made in Sweden. We use by to say who did the action: The Lord of the Rings was written by Tolkien.

reference.wrong: The Mona Lisa painted by Leonardo.
reference.right: The Mona Lisa was painted by Leonardo.
reference.why: The passive needs be + past participle.
Use by to say who did the action.

exercises.situation: You are a classmate in an English class (level: pre-intermediate). You have both studied these inventions: guns, glasses, the hot-air balloon, stamps, the saxophone, dynamite, the wristwatch, the mobile phone, Lego, CDs, the dishwasher, nappies, windscreen wipers, the life raft, the solar-heated house and the home security system. Ask: Which three of these inventions do you think are the most important? Why? Which ones could you live without? Do you know who invented them or where they were invented? Ask follow-up questions and give your own opinion too: for you, the mobile phone, glasses and the dishwasher are the most important, and you could live without Lego and CDs. Use the passive naturally in your answers (was invented by…) and gently repeat the correct form if the student makes a mistake with the passive.

reference.title: File 9
reference.text: Second conditional: if + past simple, would / wouldn’t + infinitive for imaginary situations: If a bear attacked me, I’d run away. If I were you, I wouldn’t buy it. Present perfect + for / since to say how long: I’ve lived here for ten years / since 2015. How long have you had this car? Present perfect or past simple: I was married for 15 years (finished) – I’ve been married for 15 years (still married).

reference.title: File 10
reference.text: Expressing movement: verb + preposition (went into, came out of, ran across, along, down, over, past, through, towards). Phrasal verbs: with some, a pronoun goes between the verb and the particle: Pick it up (not Pick up it); with others it doesn’t: look for them, look after him. The passive: am / is / are or was / were + past participle: The watch was invented by the Swiss.

tasks.context:
Bad losers? The hardest lesson to learn in sport is how to lose like a true sportsperson, without blaming your defeat on others. Here are some famous moments when losing was just too hard…

Nelson Piquet. In the 1982 German Grand Prix, the Brazilian driver Nelson Piquet crashed into the Chilean driver Eliseo Salazar and had to leave the race. Piquet was so angry that he got out of his car, ran towards Salazar, and tried to hit and kick him.

Ahn Jung-Hwan and Luciano Gaucci. When South Korea beat Italy in the 2002 World Cup, the winning goal was scored by Ahn Jung-Hwan, who played for the Italian club Perugia. The club’s owner, Luciano Gaucci, was furious: ‘That gentleman will never set foot in Perugia again… I have no intention of paying a salary to somebody who has ruined Italian football.’ Gaucci later apologized, but Ahn never went back to an Italian club.

Jon Drummond. At the 2003 World Athletics Championships, the American sprinter Jon Drummond was disqualified for a false start. He refused to leave, lay down on the track, and cried. Later his coach said, ‘He’s still crying. We’re making him drink water because he’s becoming dehydrated.’

Angel Matos. At the 2008 Beijing Olympics, the Cuban tae kwon do fighter Angel Matos was disqualified in the bronze medal match. He kicked the referee in the head and attacked a Swedish judge. He was banned for life.

Robert Bauer. At the 2016 Rio Olympics, when the Brazilian crowd booed the German football team, the German player Robert Bauer showed the fans seven fingers to remind them of Germany’s 7–1 win over Brazil in the 2014 World Cup semi-final.

exercises.situation: A friendly revision chat in an English class (level: pre-intermediate) after Files 9 and 10. Check that the student can do these things, one by one, with short questions and reactions: 1) say what they would do if a dog attacked them, if they won the lottery, and if they had more free time; 2) say how long they have lived where they live now, had their laptop or phone, and been at their school or job; 3) tell you their life story briefly (where they were born, school, important moments); 4) say three things you have to do in some sports, using a verb and a preposition of movement (e.g. in golf you hit the ball into the hole); 5) say true sentences with take off, turn down and look after; 6) say when three things were invented or built. At the end ask which sportsperson from the article ‘Bad losers?’ (Nelson Piquet, Luciano Gaucci, Jon Drummond, Angel Matos, Robert Bauer) they think behaved the worst and why. Keep it natural, one question at a time; if the student makes a mistake with the second conditional, for / since, the present perfect, prepositions of movement, phrasal verb word order or the passive, repeat the correct form naturally in your reply.

exercises.opener: Hi! Let’s see what you remember from Files 9 and 10. First question: what would you do if a big dog attacked you?
criteria: uses the second conditional correctly (If I…, I’d…)
uses the present perfect with for and since correctly
tells a life story with the past simple
uses verbs + prepositions of movement and phrasal verbs with correct word order
uses the passive to say when things were invented or built

steps.text: Say what you would do in three situations
steps.example: If a dog attacked me, I’d stand still. If I won the lottery, I’d travel.

steps.text: Say how long you have had or done things
steps.example: I’ve lived in this flat for five years. I’ve had my phone since 2023.
I was born in 1995. I went to school in Kazan, and I moved to Moscow in 2017.

steps.text: Describe three things in a sport
steps.example: In football you kick the ball into the goal. In the high jump you jump over the bar.

steps.text: Say sentences with take off, turn down and look after
steps.example: I take off my shoes at home. I look after my little brother.

steps.text: Say when three things were invented or built
steps.example: The telephone was invented in 1876. The Eiffel Tower was built in 1889.

steps.text: Say who behaved worst in ‘Bad losers?’
steps.example: I think Angel Matos behaved worst because he kicked the referee.
